rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Under the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) rules, your employer may not employ you in the last six weeks before the birth. The law calls this the "Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung" (protection period before the birth). An exception applies if you expressly declare that you are willing to work, and you can withdraw that declaration at any time for the future.

The six weeks are counted from the expected date of birth, "wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme oder eines Entbindungspflegers ergibt". That means the date on a certificate from a doctor or midwife, not a date you estimate yourself. Six weeks before 15 November 2026 is 4 October 2026. The excerpts do not say exactly how the first day of the period is counted, so check the start date against the date on your certificate with your employer.

If the baby is not born on the expected day, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match.

After the birth, your employer may not employ you until eight weeks have passed. This extends to twelve weeks in three cases:
1. a premature birth
2. a multiple birth
3. a disability in the child, diagnosed by a doctor before the eight weeks end. In this case the extension applies only if you apply for it.

If the baby comes early, the period after the birth is extended by the time that was cut from the period before it.

Self-employed women are not covered by the Mutterschutz law.

The excerpts do not name an authority that confirms these dates for you.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law sets no fixed application deadline. It limits how far back payment reaches. Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen"). It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the start of the month of life in which your application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist". Months of the child's life earlier than those three are not paid. What counts is the month in which the application arrives, not the month in which you send it.

Elterngeld can be received from the day of birth ("ab dem Tag der Geburt"). Basiselterngeld can be received until the child completes the 14th month of life. Elterngeld Plus can be received until the child completes the 32nd month of life, as long as at least one parent receives it in consecutive months from the 15th month of life onward.

Whether and how much Elterngeld your family receives is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for you, not by this summary.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is not applied for. You request it from your employer in text form. The notice period depends on when the leave falls.

- Leave before the child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
- Leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year: at least 13 weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

Both periods are counted back from the start of the leave, and the request must be made "in Textform" (in text form). The Familienportal explains that text form includes a letter without a signature or an email.

If you request leave that falls before the third birthday, you must say at the same time which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit ("für welche Zeiten innerhalb von zwei Jahren Elternzeit genommen werden soll").

Shorter notice is possible as an exception for urgent reasons ("Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich"). The law does not set a figure for this shorter period. The Familienportal says it depends on the individual case and gives premature birth as an example.

If a mother cannot request leave directly after her maternity protection period in time, for a reason that is not her fault, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends.

Your employer must confirm your Elternzeit to you in writing ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen").

The Familienportal also says that for children born before 1 July 2015, seven weeks' notice applies to all Elternzeit, including leave after the third birthday. The statutory provision behind that rule is not in the excerpts I have. Whether it applies to your child is a question for your employer. If there is a dispute, the labour courts decide.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
After the birth, Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) normally lasts eight weeks. The law says the employer may not employ a woman "bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung" (until eight weeks after the birth).

An early birth can lengthen this in two separate ways.

1. Days lost before the birth are added after it. The period before the birth is six weeks, counted from the expected due date. If the baby arrives before that date, the period before the birth is shortened. The law then lengthens the period after the birth "um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung" (by the length of that shortening). The guidance page puts it this way: the total period still comes to 14 weeks.

2. The period after the birth becomes twelve weeks instead of eight in three cases:
- "bei Frühgeburten" (premature births),
- "bei Mehrlingsgeburten" (multiple births such as twins), and
- where a disability in the child is medically established before the end of the eight weeks after the birth. This third extension applies only if the woman applies for it. The guidance page says this application goes to the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse).

Both rules can apply together. For a premature birth, the law extends the twelve-week period as well by the days lost before the birth. The twelve-week extension does not apply to a stillbirth.

Not every early birth counts as a "Frühgeburt". The guidance page describes it as a birth so early that it counts medically as premature, and gives the example of a birth weight under 2,500 grams. The statute excerpt does not define the term.

During these protection periods, Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay) is paid for the period before the birth, the period after it and the day of birth itself. Women in statutory health insurance receive it under the health insurance rules. Women outside statutory insurance receive it from the federal government, at most 210 euros in total. The Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung pays it on application.

Whether a particular birth counts as premature, and how long your own period runs, is not something these excerpts decide. Your Krankenkasse can tell you for your case, or the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung if you are not in statutory health insurance.

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
In general, no. Under § 17 of the Maternity Protection Act (MuSchG), dismissal by the employer is not permitted ("Die Kündigung gegenüber einer Frau ist unzulässig") in three periods:
1. during pregnancy;
2. until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy;
3. until the end of the protection period after the birth, and at least until four months after the birth.

This Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies only if one of two conditions is met. Either the employer knew of the pregnancy, miscarriage or birth when giving notice, or you tell the employer within two weeks after receiving the notice ("innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach Zugang der Kündigung"). Missing the two weeks does no harm if the delay was for a reason you are not responsible for and you inform the employer without delay. The same rules apply to steps the employer takes to prepare a dismissal.

There is a narrow exception. The highest state authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, may in special cases declare a dismissal permissible. This is only possible where the case is not connected with your condition during pregnancy, after a miscarriage or after the birth. Such a dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The official family portal lists examples: insolvency, partial closure of the business, a small business that cannot continue without a qualified replacement, or a particularly serious breach of duty. It also states that without the authority's approval the dismissal is invalid ("Ohne die Zustimmung der Aufsichtsbehörde ist die Kündigung unwirksam").

If you are dismissed without that approval, the same portal says you must bring a claim before the labour court. It says this must "normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen" (normally within 3 weeks) be done, counted from receipt of the written notice. It says that if no claim is brought, the dismissal is treated as legally effective.

If you take parental leave after the birth, separate dismissal protection under § 18 of the Federal Parental Allowance and Parental Leave Act (BEEG) can apply.

Whether a particular dismissal is permitted is decided by the state occupational-safety supervisory authority and, if it comes to it, the labour court.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Federal law sets a limit based on zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income), not gross pay. Above it, there is no Elterngeld (parental allowance) at all.

The statute says the entitlement lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the person had taxable income of more than 175,000 euros ("in Höhe von mehr als 175 000 Euro") in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth ("im letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes"). If another person also meets the conditions for Elterngeld, the limit applies to both together. The entitlement lapses if the combined taxable income of both persons is more than 175,000 euros (BEEG §1(8)).

Taxable income is not the same as gross income. The official guidance page says gross income is usually considerably higher, because certain expenses, allowances and deductions are subtracted first. The taxable income is set by the Finanzamt (tax office) and shown in the tax assessment notice (Steuerbescheid).

When the tax assessment for that period is not yet available at the time of application, the law still allows an application. If the information in the application indicates the limit will not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation ("unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs"). It can be withdrawn if the limit turns out to be exceeded (BEEG §8(2)). Where it cannot yet be said whether the limit is exceeded, the amount is decided provisionally ("vorläufig") until the evidence is provided (BEEG §8(3)).

The 175,000 euro figure is the one the statute states now. The official guidance page says different, higher limits applied to earlier births. The transitional provision that governs earlier births is not among the excerpts. Which limit applies to a particular birth is decided by the parental allowance office for your district. Only that office decides whether the limit affects your own application.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
The law sets the number of months for both parents together. It does not decide how many months your family will receive. That is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for your district.

Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid in monthly amounts for the child's months of life, counted from the birth date, not for calendar months (BEEG §4(2)). It comes in two forms: basic Elterngeld ('Basiselterngeld') and 'Elterngeld Plus' (BEEG §4(1)).

Basic months for both parents together:
- Parents jointly have 12 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld: 'Die Eltern haben gemeinsam Anspruch auf zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld' (BEEG §4(3)).
- Two further months ('Partnermonate') are added if one parent's earned income is reduced in two months of the child's life. That gives 14 in total (BEEG §4(3)).

Swapping for Elterngeld Plus:
- Instead of one month of basic Elterngeld, a parent can take two months of Elterngeld Plus: 'jeweils zwei Lebensmonate Elterngeld Plus' (BEEG §4(3)).

Limits per parent:
- One parent can have at most 12 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld. On top of that come at most four monthly amounts of 'Partnerschaftsbonus' under §4b (BEEG §4(4)). The conditions for the Partnerschaftsbonus are set in §4b, which is not in the excerpts here.
- A parent only has a claim if they take Elterngeld for at least two months (BEEG §4(4)).

Time windows:
- Basic Elterngeld can be drawn until the child completes its 14th month of life (BEEG §4(1)).
- Elterngeld Plus can be drawn until the child completes its 32nd month of life. From the 15th month, at least one parent must take it in consecutive months (BEEG §4(1)).

Premature births. The joint total of basic Elterngeld is higher if the child was born:
- at least 6 weeks before the expected delivery date: 13 months;
- at least 8 weeks before: 14 months;
- at least 12 weeks before: 15 months;
- at least 16 weeks before: 16 months.

In these cases, the per-parent maximum and the time windows are extended to match (BEEG §4(5)). The expected delivery date is the one shown in the doctor's or midwife's certificate (BEEG §4(5)).

This is federal law. Whether your family meets the conditions, and how many months you receive, is decided only by the Elterngeld office responsible for your district. That office can give binding information about your case.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) gives each parent extra months of the Plus form of parental allowance when both parents work part-time at the same time. The statute calls it a "zusätzlichen Monatsbetrag Elterngeld Plus", an additional monthly amount (BEEG §4b(1)).

Conditions the law sets (BEEG §4b):
- Both parents work "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats": at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week, averaged over the month of the child's life.
- Both parents meet the general conditions of BEEG §1. The excerpts do not reproduce §1, so they do not say what those conditions are.
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts. It can only be claimed for at least two months of the child's life.
- Both parents must take it at the same time and in consecutive months of the child's life.
- Under §4b(5), the consecutive-months requirement still counts as met if it later turns out the conditions were not met in every month applied for.

One parent alone (BEEG §4c). A single parent can receive these additional monthly amounts by working 24 to 32 hours a week on average in two to four consecutive months of the child's life. This applies if one of three grounds exists:
1. The parent meets the conditions for the single-parent tax relief under §24b(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, and the other parent lives with neither them nor the child.
2. Care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) of the Civil Code.
3. Care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count.

If one of these grounds arises while both parents are already receiving the bonus, one parent can continue receiving it (§4b(4)).

Amount. The federal family portal says the bonus is calculated the same way as the Plus form of parental allowance. Depending on income before the birth, it is between 150 and 900 euros per parent per month.

The portal also says its explanations cover children born after August 2021. For children born before 1 September 2021, some rules differ, and parents should ask their Elterngeldstelle.

Whether a particular family qualifies, and for how much, is decided by the responsible Elterngeldstelle.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid backdated for at most six months. The law says payment is made "rückwirkend nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist". This means retroactively only for the last six months before the start of the month in which the application is received. Months further back than that are not paid out.

The same section adds that the underlying entitlement is "von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt". The six-month limit restricts what is paid out. It does not remove the entitlement itself.

Because the six months are counted back from the month the application arrives, each month of delay moves that window forward.

Kindergeld must be applied for in writing at the responsible family benefits office. The official family portal says to submit it to the family benefits office of your local employment agency. To claim backdated payment, the portal says to state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when you want Kindergeld.

Whether you were entitled for those months, and how many months are paid, is decided by the family benefits office. That office handles the application. Questions about applying can go to the Federal Employment Agency's free service line, 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?

Kindergeld (child benefit) is set by federal law at 259 euros per month for each child. The statute says "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro" (Kindergeld is 259 euros per month for each child). The law does not set a different amount for a first child.

Kindergeld is paid monthly from the start of the month in which the conditions are met, until the end of the month in which they stop being met. For example, for a child born on 25 May, the full Kindergeld is paid for May.

This is the amount the law sets. Whether your family is entitled is decided by the Familienkasse, not by this service.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The birth must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) responsible for the place where the child was born within one week. The Personenstandsgesetz says the birth is to be reported to that office "binnen einer Woche" (within one week). The report can be made orally or in writing by the persons the law names, or in writing by the institution where the birth took place. If a child is stillborn, the report must be made at the latest on the third working day after the birth.

If your child is born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the institution notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the birth confirmation. If your child is born at home, the midwife or doctor issues the birth confirmation, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

A separate period applies to the name. You give your child's name when the birth is registered. If you have not decided on a name yet, you must report it to the Standesamt within one month. After that, the Standesamt must inform the family court, which then chooses one parent to decide the name.

The excerpts do not say what other documents you need. The familienportal says these are listed on the website of the Standesamt for the place where your child is born.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
Yes. Federal law gives a woman insured with a Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer) an entitlement to the help of a Hebamme (midwife) during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth. The statute states this as "Anspruch auf ärztliche Betreuung sowie auf Hebammenhilfe". That includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and prenatal check-ups.

After the birth, the Hebamme's postnatal care is covered until twelve weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt"). Care beyond that needs a doctor's order ("weitergehende Leistungen bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung").

If the mother cannot care for the child after the birth, the insured child has its own entitlement to the Hebamme's care that relates to the child.

If you are privately insured, this rule does not apply in the same way. Ask your private insurer which services it covers before you rely on them.

Whether a particular service is covered in your own case is decided by your Krankenkasse. Contact it for a binding answer.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The schedule of children's check-ups is set by the Kinder-Richtlinie (children's guideline) of the Gemeinsamer Bundesausschuss. It provides ten check-ups in the first six years of life ("insgesamt zehn Untersuchungen"). It also says the check-ups can only be used within their set time windows, including a tolerance period ("können nur in den jeweils angegebenen Zeiträumen unter Berücksichtigung folgender Toleranzgrenzen in Anspruch genommen werden").

The first check-ups are:

- U1: immediately after birth ("Unmittelbar nach der Geburt"). It should take place within the first 30 minutes after the birth ("innerhalb der ersten 30 Minuten nach der Geburt"). If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: from the 3rd to the 10th day of life ("3.-10. Lebenstag"). The tolerance window is the 3rd to the 14th day.
- U3: in the 4th to 5th week of life ("4.-5. Lebenswoche"). The tolerance window is the 3rd to the 8th week.
- U4: in the 3rd to 4th month of life ("3.-4. Lebensmonat"). The tolerance window is the 2nd to the 4½th month.

The later check-ups run up to the U9, at 60 to 64 months.

For babies born early, the same time windows still apply ("Auch bei Frühgeborenen sind die Untersuchungszeiträume einzuhalten"). The early birth is taken into account when the results are assessed.

Under the guideline, children are entitled to these early-detection check-ups until they turn 18.

The G-BA's page notes that the version of the guideline it offers does not yet include a decision that came into force on 20 August 2026. If you need the current timing, check the G-BA's published version or ask your paediatrician.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth, and for the day of the birth itself.

Who pays depends on how you are insured:

- If you are a member of a statutory health insurer, you receive Mutterschaftsgeld under the rules of the statutory health insurance code. For members who are employed when the protection period before the birth begins, it is based on average net daily pay over the last three settled calendar months before that period, and is at most 13 euros per calendar day. Other members receive it at the level of sickness benefit.
- If you are employed, your employer pays a supplement covering the difference between 13 euros and your average net daily pay over the same three months.
- If you are not a member of a statutory health insurer, you receive Mutterschaftsgeld paid by the federal government, at most 210 euros in total. The law says this is paid "auf Antrag" (on application) by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (Federal Office for Social Security).

The protection periods normally begin 6 weeks before the expected due date and end 8 weeks after the birth. For payment before the birth, the deciding document is a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected date of delivery. The claim is suspended for as long as you receive pay that is subject to contributions. One-off payments do not count.

Mutterschaftsgeld from the statutory health insurer and the employer supplement are offset against Elterngeld (parental allowance) for the period from the day of the birth. The 210-euro payment from the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung is not offset.

When to apply: the excerpts do not say when or how to apply if you are insured with a statutory health insurer. Your statutory health insurer can tell you its procedure. If you are not statutorily insured, the application goes to the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung. Whether you qualify, and for how much, is decided by your health insurer or the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No, not automatically. Under German law, a man becomes the legal father of a child in one of three ways (BGB §1592): he is married to the mother at the time of the birth ("zum Zeitpunkt der Geburt mit der Mutter des Kindes verheiratet"); he has acknowledged paternity ("die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat"); or a court has determined his paternity ("gerichtlich festgestellt").

If the parents are not married at the time of the birth, the father must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to be the legal father. It is voluntary and needs the mother's consent. A court can also determine paternity.

What the law attaches to the Vaterschaftsanerkennung:
- It can be made before the child is born ("schon vor der Geburt des Kindes zulässig", BGB §1594(4)).
- It is not effective while another man's paternity exists ("solange die Vaterschaft eines anderen Mannes besteht", BGB §1594(2)). For example, if the mother is married to another man at the time of the birth, her husband is the legal father.
- It is invalid if made subject to a condition or a time limit (BGB §1594(3)).
- The father must make the declaration in person at a competent office, for example the Jugendamt, a Standesamt, an Amtsgericht or a notary. The mother must also give her consent in person. Depending on the federal state, a notary or Amtsgericht may charge a fee.

Being the legal father does not on its own give parental custody. For unmarried parents, the mother has custody from the birth. For the father to share it, both parents must also declare that they want joint custody, or a court must decide. Marrying after the birth also establishes joint custody.

Your local Jugendamt advises on paternity and parental custody.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
Under German law, if the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, the mother has parental custody. The parents get joint custody in any of three ways:

1. Both parents declare that they want to take on custody together. Each parent makes a Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody).
2. The parents marry each other.
3. The family court transfers joint custody to them.

Before the father can share custody, he must first be legally recognised as the father. This happens when he acknowledges the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Acknowledging paternity does not give him custody by itself. A Sorgeerklärung or a court decision is still needed.

The declarations can be made, for example, at the youth welfare office or before a notary. They can also be made before the birth.

If the parents do not both make declarations, one parent can apply to the family court. The court transfers joint custody, or part of it, to both parents if this does not conflict with the child's welfare. If the other parent gives no reasons against it, and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes joint custody does not conflict with the child's welfare. In that case, the family court decides in a simplified procedure. It does not hear the youth welfare office and does not hear the parents in person.

Your local youth welfare office advises on all questions about parental custody.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Frankfurt?
rows.reply:
The law does not name one office for the whole country. Under BEEG §12, each state decides which authorities handle Elterngeld (parental allowance). The responsible one is the authority for the district where your child has its residence in Germany when you first apply ("des Bezirks, in dem das Kind ... zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat").

In practice, this means you apply to the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) responsible for your child's place of residence. You can apply in person at that office or online. Every state offers an online application, and in many states the ElterngeldDigital service guides you through it.

For Hessen, the Elterngeld page of the Regierungspräsidium Gießen lists the contact details of the six Hessian offices for this area, and of the body that supervises Elterngeld. That page also refers to applying online and on paper. The excerpts do not say which of the six offices covers Frankfurt. Use that contact list, or ask the Elterngeldstelle for your district, which can give you binding information.

Two rules from the statute matter when you apply. The application must be made in writing ("schriftlich"). Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received, so applying later loses whole months of payment.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Berlin?
rows.reply:
You apply to the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) responsible for where your child lives.

Who is responsible: the federal law leaves it to each state to designate the offices that handle Elterngeld (parental allowance). The responsible office is the one the state has designated for the district where the child has its residence in Germany when you first apply ("des Bezirks, in dem das Kind ... zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat"). The excerpts I have do not name the individual Berlin offices. The Service Berlin page for this service is the place to find the one for your district.

Form of the application: Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). The application is signed by the parent making it and, to confirm awareness, also by the other entitled parent, except where one person has sole custody or in the case of § 4c. In the application you state for which months you are claiming Basiselterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or Partnerschaftsbonus.

Ways to apply in Berlin:
- Online: Service Berlin offers online application. To use it, you log in with a BundID account, or register for one. rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not in every case. German law ties citizenship at birth to specific conditions, and which side of them your family falls on is decided by the authorities, not by this answer.

By descent: under StAG §4(1), a child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) by birth "wenn ein Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzt", meaning if one parent holds German citizenship.

By birth in Germany: under StAG §4(3), a child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth if one parent meets both of these conditions:
1. has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland"), and
2. holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss citizen or a Swiss citizen's family member, a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.
The acquisition is entered in the birth register where the child's birth is recorded.

If the child does not acquire German citizenship, AufenthG §33 sets out the child's residence status:
- A child born in Germany may be granted a residence permit by the authorities on their own initiative if one parent holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a Niederlassungserlaubnis or an Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU.
- If, at the time of birth, both parents hold one of these, the residence permit is granted to the child on the authorities' own initiative ("wird ... von Amts wegen erteilt").
- If the mother or father holds a visa, or may stay without a visa, at the time of birth, the child's stay counts as permitted until the visa or the lawful visa-free stay ends.

Whether your child meets these conditions is decided by the responsible authorities. The excerpts do not name them. Your local Ausländerbehörde (foreigners' authority) can give binding information about your own residence status and your child's. The excerpts do not cover Indian citizenship rules for your child. The Indian embassy or consulate responsible for your area handles that question.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
It depends on the parents' status. Only the authority can decide it for your child, but the law sets out these rules.

Residence permit rules for a child born in Germany (AufenthG §33):
- If one parent holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit), a settlement permit ("Niederlassungserlaubnis") or an EU long-term residence permit ("Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU"), the child can be granted an Aufenthaltserlaubnis by the authority on its own initiative. The statute says "kann ... von Amts wegen eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis erteilt werden".
- If, at the time of birth, both parents hold one of those permits, the child is granted the Aufenthaltserlaubnis on the authority's own initiative ("wird ... von Amts wegen erteilt"). The same applies where the parent with sole custody holds one.
- If the mother or father holds a visa at the time of birth, or is allowed to stay without a visa, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends ("gilt bis zum Ablauf des Visums oder des rechtmäßigen visumfreien Aufenthalts als erlaubt").

German citizenship by birth (StAG §4):
- A child acquires German citizenship at birth if one parent is a German citizen.
- A child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German citizenship if one parent meets both of these conditions. First, the parent has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland"). Second, the parent holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss citizen or a family member of one, a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.
- This acquisition is entered in the birth register where the birth is recorded.

The excerpts do not set out the application steps or say which rule applies to your child. Your local Ausländerbehörde (foreigners' authority) decides residence questions for your child and can give you binding information about your own case.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, as a general rule. The law credits Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) against Elterngeld (parental allowance). That means it is deducted from the Elterngeld, not paid on top of it.

What the law counts. BEEG §3(1) lists the income that is credited against Elterngeld. It includes:
- Mutterschaftsgeld paid under the Fifth Book of the Social Code, which is the statutory health insurance scheme.
- The employer's top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §20.

Both count only for the period from the child's birth: "die der berechtigten Person für die Zeit ab dem Tag der Geburt des Kindes zustehen".

One exception. The one-off Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §19(2) is not credited: "mit Ausnahme des Mutterschaftsgeldes nach § 19 Absatz 2 des Mutterschutzgesetzes". This is the payment of at most 210 euros, made by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer.

Part months. If the payments cover only part of a month of the child's life, they are credited only against the matching part of the Elterngeld: "sind sie nur auf den entsprechenden Teil des Elterngeldes anzurechnen" (BEEG §3(1)). The official Familienportal explains it this way. Mutterschaftsleistungen are calculated in days, so they are credited to the exact day. For the remaining days of that month, Elterngeld is paid pro rata.

What the official guidance says about the effect. For the same child, Mutterschaftsleistungen are credited in full ("komplett auf das Elterngeld angerechnet"). If they are higher than the Elterngeld, only the Mutterschaftsleistungen are paid. If the Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld. Months in which Mutterschaftsleistungen are due for the same child count as months of Basiselterngeld, even if they are due for only one day of that month.

For Mutterschaftsleistungen received for a different child, the guidance says they are credited only against part of the Elterngeld. They are not credited against 300 euros in Basiselterngeld months, or 150 euros in ElterngeldPlus months.

The guidance also says the mother's Mutterschaftsleistungen are credited only against the mother's Elterngeld, not against the father's: "nur auf das Elterngeld der Mutter".

This is the general rule. It is not a figure for your family. Only the Elterngeld office for your district decides how the crediting applies in your case and what is paid. That office can give binding information about your own case.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows some work, but not full-time work. One of the conditions in the statute for Elterngeld (parental allowance) is that the person "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt", meaning they do no paid work or no full-time paid work (BEEG §1(1) no. 4).

The official family portal says you may work part-time while receiving Elterngeld if you work "nicht mehr als 32 Stunden pro Woche" (no more than 32 hours per week). That page says it describes the rules for children born after August 2021. For children born before 1 September 2021, it says some different rules apply and that you should contact your Elterngeld office.

Working affects the amount. Under BEEG §2(3), for months after the birth in which your earnings are on average lower than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as a percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this calculation, income before the birth counts up to at most 2,770 euros ("höchstens der Betrag von 2 770 Euro").

What this means for your application:
- If your application states that you expect to earn income during the payment period, the amount is decided provisionally at first (BEEG §8(3) no. 3). After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual earnings for that time (BEEG §8(1)).
- If your application states that you expect no earnings, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation ("unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs") in case you do have earnings after all (BEEG §8(2)).
- The family portal lists the proof it expects. Employees need a certificate from their employer showing their working hours during the Elterngeld period. Self-employed people need their own statement of their previous working hours and their hours during the Elterngeld period.

Your Elterngeld office decides whether you qualify and how much you receive.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Who receives it: Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid for each child to only one person. If the child lives in the parents' shared household, the parents decide between themselves which of them is the entitled person ("bestimmen diese untereinander den Berechtigten"). If they make no decision, the family court decides on application (BKGG §3).

Where to apply: the law says the application should be made at the Familienkasse responsible under §13 ("bei der nach § 13 zuständigen Familienkasse", BKGG §9). That is the Familienkasse for the district where the entitled person has their residence ("in deren Bezirk der Berechtigte seinen Wohnsitz hat"). The same Familienkasse receives the application and decides the claim (BKGG §13). The Familienportal tells you to submit the application to the Familienkasse of your Agentur für Arbeit (employment agency).

Who may apply: besides the entitled person, anyone with a legitimate interest in the payment may apply ("wer ein berechtigtes Interesse an der Leistung des Kindergeldes hat", BKGG §9).

How to apply:
- The statute requires a written application ("schriftlich zu beantragen", BKGG §9).
- The Familienportal says you can apply electronically or in writing, using the Familienkassen's form. You can fill it in online, then print and sign it.
- For newborn children, you can apply fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, without printing or signing by hand.
- In the application you must give your tax identification number and your child's tax identification number.
- For a child under 18, the Federal Employment Agency says you normally only need to give these two tax identification numbers. For a child born abroad, it asks for a copy of the foreign birth certificate, or another official document certifying the birth.
- If the Familienkasse needs more documents, it will tell you the deadline. Missing that deadline can delay your application or lead to its refusal.

Applying late: the Familienportal says Kindergeld can be paid retroactively for up to 6 months ("für bis zu 6 Monate rückwirkend"), if it was due but not paid. To claim this, state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when.

Whether you are entitled is decided by the Familienkasse. For questions about applying, the Federal Employment Agency's free service line is 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Elterngeld (parental allowance) is federal law, so the rules below apply in Bavaria as everywhere in Germany. Bavarian procedures, such as which office handles applications there and what it asks for, are not covered here.

Who can claim. Under BEEG §1, a person is entitled if they meet all four conditions: they live or usually stay in Germany, live in one household with the child, care for and bring up the child themselves, and do no paid work or no full-time paid work ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt").

How self-employed income counts. Under BEEG §2, Elterngeld is 67 percent of income from work before the birth. That income includes positive earnings from "Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit" (farming and forestry, a trade or business, and self-employed work), after deductions for tax and social contributions. Only earnings taxable in Germany count, as a monthly average over the assessment period. The percentage rises toward 100 percent where pre-birth income was below 1,000 euros, and falls to as low as 65 percent where it was above 1,200 euros. The maximum is 1,800 euros a month and the minimum is 300 euros, including for someone with no income before the birth. If you earn less after the birth than before, Elterngeld is paid on the difference, counting at most 2,770 euros of pre-birth income. BEEG §2c covers income from employment only. The excerpts do not include the provision on how self-employed earnings are worked out in detail.

Provisional payment and proof. Under BEEG §8, the amount is decided provisionally, based on the information you have made credible, in any of these three cases: the tax assessment for the last completed tax year before the birth is not yet available and it cannot yet be said whether the amounts in §1 Absatz 8 are exceeded; pre-birth income cannot be determined; or you expect to have income from work while receiving Elterngeld. If your application stated expected income, you must prove your actual income for that period once it ends. If you stated you would have no income, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case you do have income. Payment is also subject to revocation if the tax assessment is missing and the §1 Absatz 8 amounts turn out to be exceeded.

How long. Under BEEG §4, the basic allowance can be drawn until the child completes its 14th month of life. Parents together have 12 monthly amounts, plus 2 more if one parent's income from work falls in two months. One parent can claim at most 12 monthly amounts plus up to 4 partnership bonus amounts, and must claim for at least two months. One month of the basic allowance can be taken instead as two months of Elterngeld Plus. Longer periods apply to children born early.

Only the Elterngeld office responsible for your district decides your entitlement and amount. It is the place to get binding information about your own case.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. The entries on the form are decisions and statements about your own family, and only the responsible authority assesses them. What the law and official guidance say the application has to contain is set out below.

What the application must contain:
- It must be made in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen", BEEG §7(1)).
- It must state which months of the child's life you are claiming basic Elterngeld for, which months Elterngeld Plus, and which months the partnership bonus (BEEG §7(1)).
- It must be signed by the person applying. The other entitled parent also signs, to confirm they have seen it. This does not apply in the case of §4c or where one person has sole custody (BEEG §7(3)).
- The other entitled parent can, at the same time, either make their own application, or tell the authority how many monthly amounts they claim if their claim would otherwise exceed the legal maximum (BEEG §7(3)). If neither is on file, all monthly amounts are paid to the parent who applied. The other parent can then only receive the months that remain from the total (BEEG §7(3)).

Timing: Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received (BEEG §7(1)). Months earlier than that are not paid.

Changing your choices: decisions made in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period (BEEG §7(2)). A change can reach back only three months before the month the change request is received. Where monthly amounts have already been paid, a change is not allowed except in cases of particular hardship. One exception: for a month in which Elterngeld Plus was already received, basic Elterngeld can be claimed afterwards (BEEG §7(2)).

Documents: the official family portal lists these:
- your child's birth certificate
- proof of your previous income

For employees, the income proof is:
- for mothers: pay slips for the 12 months before the month maternity protection begins
- for fathers: pay slips for the 12 months before the birth

For self-employed people, it is usually the last tax assessment. Further documents may be needed depending on the individual case (Familienportal FAQ).

Who decides and where to go: the competent authority is the one designated by the federal state for the district where the child has its residence in Germany at the time of the first application (BEEG §12(1)). That Elterngeld office for your district decides your application. It can give you binding information about how to complete it.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
Only the Elterngeld office can decide whether your application will be approved. This service cannot assess your situation or predict the outcome.

What the law says in general: under BEEG §1(1), a person is entitled to Elterngeld (parental allowance) if they meet all four of these conditions:
1. they have their residence or habitual abode in Germany ("einen Wohnsitz oder seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt in Deutschland"),
2. they live in one household with their child,
3. they care for and bring up this child themselves, and
4. they do no paid work, or do not work full-time ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit").

For multiple births there is only one entitlement. BEEG §1(2) to (4) extend entitlement to certain other groups. These are people posted abroad under German social insurance or public service, development workers and certain missionaries, and some Germans working temporarily at international bodies. They also include people caring for a child they are adopting, a spouse's child, or a child whose paternity is not yet legally settled. Finally, they cover relatives up to the third degree where the parents cannot care for the child because of serious illness, severe disability or death.

Under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

Who decides: whether you meet these conditions is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for your district. That office can give you binding information about your own case.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
How much tax your family would save by changing tax class is a calculation about your own case. This service cannot make it. Tax class choices and their tax effects belong to your local tax office or a licensed tax adviser, who can give binding information about your situation.

What the excerpts do cover is how a change of tax class before the birth is treated when parental allowance is calculated. This is federal law and applies everywhere in Germany.

- The law deducts income tax using your tax class and, where one applies, your tax factor. Tax class VI is ignored: "die Steuerklasse VI bleibt unberücksichtigt" (BEEG §2e(3)).
- If you changed tax class before the birth, the simplified net-income calculation uses the newest tax class: "kommt es auf die neueste Steuerklasse an".
- The older tax class is used only if it applied for longer than the newer one within the whole assessment period: "wenn diese innerhalb des gesamten Bemessungszeitraums länger gegolten hat als die neuere".
- Changing tax class again after the birth has no further effect on parental allowance: "hat also keine Auswirkung mehr auf Ihr Elterngeld".

The parental allowance office calculates the net income figure itself, using a simplified method. It decides the amount in any individual case. The parental allowance office for your district can give binding information about your application.
